solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Dash across sports field with end of spear in rump?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept
one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

blocks.note: rump is a cut of steak
the final letter of spear

explanation.surface: A spearman, wounded in the backside, bolts across a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: Rump looks like a body part, but it is the cut of beef, rump steak.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked across a public place, classically a pitch during a match.

clue.text: Not much fun, Europeans ditching leader? Get stuck in!

indicators.note: only a little of the word is kept, so most of its tail is cut away
to ditch the leader is to throw away the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: entertainment is fun; only its first three letters survive
the French are Europeans; their first letter goes

explanation.surface: A dour lot of continentals are urged to stop moping and throw themselves into the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrench is to dig in and establish oneself firmly, much like getting stuck in to a position.

clue.text: (& 13ac.) No successor for ex-Labour minister (one burden too many)?

blocks.note: whatever has no successor is the last
Jack Straw was Home Secretary and Foreign Secretary under Blair

explanation.surface: A former Labour cabinet member is pictured as the final straw that someone could not bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial final straw breaks the camel's back: the extra load that finally becomes unbearable.

clue.text: Maverick lone wolf overwhelming party – immediately succeeded

indicators.note: a maverick refuses to follow the herd, so these letters break out of their usual order
to overwhelm something is to swallow it up, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A rebel politician going it alone swamps the party and promptly takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that followed on came directly after, in unbroken sequence, the way a successor takes over.

clue.text: see 20ac.
Admit being involved in "awful turd" Corbyn's ultimate decline

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the letters are mangled
ultimate means final, so only the closing letter of the name counts
to be involved in something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of Corbyn
to own up is to admit

explanation.surface: A Private Eye jibe at the Labour leader, whose crude remark supposedly heralds his fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a fall in fortunes or activity, a synonym for a decline.

clue.text: Just as Cameron was, Mark's upset by Eye leader

indicators.note: in a down-the-page sense an upset word is turned over, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: to mark is to note
Ian Hislop edits Private Eye

explanation.surface: Private Eye's editor gets under the skin of an Old Etonian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Eye leader is not the letter E but the magazine's editor, Ian Hislop.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron was educated at Eton College, so he was one of its old boys.

clue.text: Posturing dictator the common people forced out

indicators.note: something forced is pushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the mob is the common people
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A strutting despot is driven from power by a popular uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Mobutu Sese Seko ruled Zaire for three decades until rebels forced him out in 1997; the grid spells him with a final O.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobutu was a notoriously vain African dictator, famous for his leopard-skin hat and grandiose posing.

clue.text: "Germany almost, almost scored – horrendous!" – usual alarmist Daily Mail?

definitions.note: describes the paper as an example of the answer

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something horrendous is a terrible mess, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline screams in horror that the Germans nearly scored.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'almost' trims one word: Germany loses its Y and scored its D.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaremonger spreads alarming stories, and Private Eye mocks the Daily Mail for its habitual panics.

clue.text: Like Woody's elaborate precautions – "sap's gone"

indicators.note: to elaborate something is to work it up anew, so the letters are reworked
whatever has gone is no longer there, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed from the longer word

explanation.surface: Woody Allen's fussy precautions are mocked as the habits of a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Allen's screen persona is the archetypal anxious, obsessive worrier, which is what neurotic describes.

clue.text: Endlessly pissed leader's inclination

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: lit is slang for drunk
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: A permanently drunk ruler is said to have a fondness for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A liking is a fondness or preference, the same as a tendency or leaning towards something.

clue.text: see 24dn.
see 3dn.
Period certain – attention held completely

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time
bound to happen means certain

explanation.surface: Someone sure of the length of a stint finds their focus totally gripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound means enthralled, as if under a magic charm that captivates the mind.

clue.text: see 24dn.
Agency encouraging disloyalty, since getting shamed – "I only screwed around"

indicators.note: screwed around suggests twisted about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheating spouse, publicly exposed, pleads that it was only a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2015 hackers leaked the user list of this affairs website, shaming millions of subscribers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashley Madison is an online dating service marketed to married people seeking affairs, so it promotes infidelity.

clue.text: Look right into Republican candidate and artfully remove him from the picture?

definitions.text: artfully remove him from the picture

indicators.note: putting one thing into another means it is inserted inside

blocks.note: an air is a look or manner
Jeb Bush was seeking the Republican nomination in 2015
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Examine the Republican hopeful properly, then quietly edit him out of the photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush is to retouch an image with a fine spray, often to erase someone unwanted.

clue.text: Old tax on wayward males that are put away regularly

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a plural noun

indicators.note: something wayward strays from its proper course, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: set in the archaic sense of an imposed levy, from setting a tax
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A historic levy is imposed on unruly men who are routinely locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' suggests prison, but here it means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Set meals are fixed-price menus served at regular sittings, and food that is eaten is informally put away.

clue.text: see 21dn.
New Englander: jerk on drugs

blocks.note: to jerk something is to yank it
E is ecstasy, so two of them make drugs in the plural

explanation.surface: An American from the north-east is dismissed as a stoned idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerk looks like an insult for a person, but it is the verb meaning to pull sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee is a native of New England in particular, though outsiders apply the name to all Americans.

clue.text: Far Left figure breaking Neil Kinnock's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
something breaking falls apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle of the seven letters of Kinnock

explanation.surface: A hard-left militant breaks the heart of Labour's former leader Neil Kinnock.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinnock famously fought the Trotskyist Militant tendency inside Labour in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin, the Bolshevik revolutionary, is an iconic hero of the far left of politics.

clue.text: (& 5dn.) Twitter flop? Engage in meaningful discussion!

blocks.note: to twitter is to chatter
a turkey is a failure, especially a show

explanation.surface: A failed tweet is held up as a call to have a proper conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Twitter looks like the social network, but it is just the verb for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk turkey is an idiom for speaking frankly and getting down to serious business.

clue.text: (& 17ac.) Sexual partner suppressing rude titter about right place for 'pussy business'?

indicators.note: something rude is rough and unrefined, so the letters are knocked about
about means around, so these letters wrap around the next piece
to suppress is to hold down and contain, so one piece goes around the rest

blocks.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A smutty innuendo about a lover's giggles and where the 'pussy business' should happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat does its business in a litter tray, and pussy is a familiar word for a cat.

clue.text: Appearing cautious initially, entering street-wise mate – a rough ride?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken
to enter something is to go inside it

blocks.note: bro is street slang for a mate
a performer appearing is on
the first letter of cautious

explanation.surface: A wary newcomer joins a streetwise pal, which promises to be a bumpy experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is a wild or half-tamed horse that bucks, giving a rider a rough time.

clue.text: Measures PM once to fit a condom?

blocks.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
Edward Heath was Conservative Prime Minister 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A bachelor former prime minister is measured up for a contraceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensheath is to enclose in a sheath, and a condom is a sheath.

clue.text: (& 14ac./12ac.) US navy is embroiled with Korea – one's going to look after number one

indicators.note: being embroiled means being tangled up, so the letters are mixed together
whatever is going is departing, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a means one, as in a dozen; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: The American fleet is drawn into a Korean conflict where everyone is out for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two As in the combined letters is dropped before the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To save your own skin is to protect yourself first, which is the idiom for putting your own interests first.

clue.text: Brown jaundiced: "Widdecombe's back, full of energy!"

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the words are read from right to left
something full of another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: Ann Widdecombe, Conservative MP, plus 's for is
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sour Gordon Brown greets the return of the lively Tory Ann Widdecombe.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like Gordon Brown, but with jaundiced it is a yellowish brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment of yellowish brown, so a brown tinged yellow as if by jaundice.

clue.text: Miliband, at heart very taken with transforming love is ... transformed

indicators.note: having something at heart means holding it in the middle
transforming changes the form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: Ed Miliband, Labour leader until 2015
V is the abbreviation for very
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband is pictured as changed, his heart taken over by love.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has evolved has developed gradually into a new form, meaning it has changed.
